chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Disc jockeys playing one thing over and over
summary: He says radio programmers plug one kind of music and should give variety, which benefits advertisers too.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah, I suppose so. But I think it's mostly due to the way the disk jockeys are playing(?).

I think somebody should get on them and tell them to change their tactics. Because they would get more listening for their...especially for their channel...now what is it...stations... Their station will have more listening. It's better for the people that are advertising, the things they're advertising, the commodities they advertise. It depends upon how many people listen to the station.
If they put good music on the air, people would listen to it.

Yeah. Well, if they can put... But put some different music! You don't have to have the same thing all the time, all through-in and throughout. Give the people a little variety. That's what you need. That's what music needs, is variety.
So you think, by and large, Radio has had a pretty bad influence on the way...
Some of the radio has had it. There's really a lot of guys who were ...(?)... But most of them have these things going, and they just do these one things, and just that's it!
It's selling some merchandise. That's what they're trying to do.

Yeah. Well, they're trying to sell that particular number or piece. But they're not thinking about their clients, who they're representing. They're likely representing cigarettes and beers, or this and that and the other. And those people that... There's a lot of people that won't listen to that channel just because; because that it sticks to one and it don't vary. You know?
